question: Find the point on the curve $y=x^2+4x$ at which the tangent has an inclination of $135^\circ$ with the positive direction of the $x$-axis.
explanation: Slope from the angle of inclinationIf a tangent makes an angle $\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis, its slope is $\tan\theta$. Therefore,$$m=\tan135^\circ=-1$$Derivative of the curve$$\frac{dy}{dx}=2x+4$$Equality of slopesAt the required point,$$2x+4=-1$$$$2x=-5\Rightarrow x=-\frac{5}{2}$$Corresponding ordinate$$y=\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)^2+4\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)$$$$y=\frac{25}{4}-10=-\frac{15}{4}$$ConclusionThe required point is $\left(-\frac{5}{2},-\frac{15}{4}\right)$.
